findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an abstract class that cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but its body is just `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares several abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). Because none are implemented, instantiating the class raises TypeError. Detector.detector_handler calls `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any Detector with type 'metric_alert_fire' will crash when its handler is built, where previously it returned an empty list. Either implement the abstract members or keep the previous non-stateful base.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate still says it 'returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method now returns a dict keyed by group key. Callers and implementers reading the docstring will expect the old contract.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe expects an occurrence whose fingerprint does not match the evaluated group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", ...)`, so its fingerprint is `<id>:val1`. The call under test is `evaluate_group_key_value("group_key", ...)`, and the hook builds the occurrence with fingerprint `<id>:group_key`. The equality assertion compares the full IssueOccurrence, so the fingerprints differ and the assertion should fail. Either the expected group key should be "val1" or the occurrence should be built with "group_key". The test also passes value 6 while the actual call uses 10, which is misleading even though the mock ignores it.
